title: deployment.set_target writes the durable target, adopting the orphaned admission module
description:
SPIDR child of task-04b3ce7e349743c2a156d32ee5550ba5, filed by architect-fa3a3e17 on 2026-09-06 on the governor's re-plan hand-back. That row measured at 18+ existing paths before its new files, past the 10-file cap, and the governor's note asks the split to "either adopt [deploy-target-contracts.ts] in the child that owns the constants or delete it from the worktree". THIS ROW ADOPTS IT.

WHY THE SPLIT FALLS HERE. `deployment.set_target` is an ORDINARY SYNCHRONOUS WRITE and `deployment.deploy` is not - bootstrap-contracts.ts:48 already records that distinction in its own comment. `CommandHandler` is `(context: HandlerContext) => ServiceOutcome` (bootstrap-ledger-vocabulary.ts:253), a SYNC type, so set_target fits GOAL_HANDLERS and deploy cannot. The parent keeps the async half.

THE ORPHAN THIS ROW ADOPTS. `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-target-contracts.ts` is UNTRACKED (`git status --porcelain` shows `??`) and `git grep -c deploy-target-contracts -- apps/daemon/src` returns ZERO IMPORTERS. It is not scratch work - it is a considered module holding the two kinds' vocabulary, the admission rules for an operator-typed target, and the aggregate the binding lands on, with its own header stating "ADMISSION IS A SECURITY BOUNDARY, NOT TIDINESS. Every field here is operator-typed text that ends up in an argv (`--network <network>`, `ssh <sshTarget> docker ...`) or on a receipt that a screen renders." That reasoning is worth keeping; an unconsumed module is not. This row gives it a consumer or the row is not done.

MEASURED AT HEAD (moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-fa3a3e17, 2026-09-06 - MOST OF THE ROSTER WORK IS ALREADY LANDED, so do not redo it:
- `daemon-command-vocabulary.ts:70` -> `"deployment.set_target": CAPABILITIES.GOAL, "deployment.deploy": CAPABILITIES.GOAL` (family table, DONE).
- `:361` -> both kinds in the operator roster, with `:358` commenting that deploy is served from an ASYNC entry (DONE).
- PAYLOAD_KEYS HAS MOVED TO ITS OWN FILE: `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-payload-keys.ts:165` -> `"deployment.set_target": ["environment", "network", "sshTarget", "url"]` and `:166` -> `"deployment.deploy": ["environment", "sha"]` (DONE). Plans naming PAYLOAD_KEYS inside daemon-command-vocabulary.ts are stale.
- `bootstrap-contracts.ts:51-52` -> both kinds listed (DONE).
So the roster is NOT this row's work. `git grep -n "deployment.set_target" -- apps/daemon/src` finds NO handler: the write itself is what is missing.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: adopting deploy-target-contracts.ts (tracked, imported, tested), the `deployment.set_target` handler in GOAL_HANDLERS, and the durable target aggregate that `deploy-ports.ts:32` already declares is "WRITTEN by `deployment.set_target`; only read here".

NOT IN SCOPE: `deployment.deploy` and its async entry, the journey, the roster counts - all the parent's.
definitionOfDone: `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-target-contracts.ts` is ADOPTED: tracked by git, imported by production code, and covered by tests. `git status --porcelain` no longer shows it as `??`, and `git grep -c deploy-target-contracts -- apps/daemon/src` returns a NONZERO importer count from a non-test module. An unconsumed module satisfies every existence grep while the feature does not exist.

`deployment.set_target` is registered as a SYNCHRONOUS handler in GOAL_HANDLERS (apps/daemon/src/goals/goal-services.ts), matching `CommandHandler = (context) => ServiceOutcome` at bootstrap-ledger-vocabulary.ts:253. It writes the durable target that deploy-ports.ts:32 declares is written by this kind and only read there. Do NOT add it to the async entries - it is an ordinary synchronous write and bootstrap-contracts.ts:48 already says so.

THE ADMISSION RULES ARE ENFORCED AND ASSERTED, because every field is operator-typed text that reaches an argv or a rendered receipt: a `url` carrying `user:password@` is REFUSED, and a `network` or `sshTarget` containing whitespace, a shell metacharacter, a newline or a NUL is REFUSED. Assert each with its specific code AND the layer that refused - never merely that it failed. The engine spawns with shell:false so a metacharacter cannot re-parse into a second command, but an unadmitted value still reaches a remote host and a credential still lands on every receipt.

THE DURABLE TARGET ROUND-TRIPS: written by the command, read back from a REAL store, with every member asserted. Setting a target twice for one environment REPLACES rather than duplicating - assert the read-back count is one.

NO ROSTER WORK. The family table, the operator roster, PAYLOAD_KEYS (now in apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-payload-keys.ts) and the bootstrap kind lists ALREADY carry both kinds - `git status --porcelain` proves daemon-command-vocabulary.ts, daemon-command-payload-keys.ts and bootstrap-contracts.ts are untouched by this row. Eight rows are contending those files; re-editing one is a collision, not thoroughness.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` covers no apps/** file, so say that rather than quoting a bare root count line.
taskRails: ADOPT THE ORPHAN OR DELETE IT - do not leave apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-target-contracts.ts untracked with zero importers. The governor's hand-back names this explicitly.
ADMISSION IS A SECURITY BOUNDARY, NOT TIDINESS. Operator-typed target text reaches an argv and a rendered receipt; a url with embedded userinfo puts a credential on every receipt.

NO ROSTER EDITS. The vocabulary, payload keys and bootstrap lists already carry both kinds and eight rows are contending those files.
NO DEPLOY EFFECT, NO JOURNEY, NO UI - all belong to the parent task-04b3ce7e349743c2a156d32ee5550ba5.

implementationPlan.description:
THE DURABLE TARGET WRITE. Create `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-target-ledger.ts` (+ its one-line `.js` bridge).

It writes the aggregate `deployTargetAggregateId(projectId, environment)` (:83) with the event `DEPLOY_TARGET_BOUND_EVENT` (:41), from an `AdmittedDeployTarget` (:87), and reads back through `decodeDeployTarget` (:117) so the write and the read share one codec rather than two hand-rolled shapes.

SETTING A TARGET TWICE FOR ONE ENVIRONMENT REPLACES, IT DOES NOT ACCUMULATE (DoD 4). The aggregate id is keyed by (projectId, environment), so the second write supersedes the first; assert the read-back count is one in step 6. An accumulating ledger would make `DeployTargetPort` ambiguous about which target is current, and the deploy engine reads exactly one.

SUPPLY THE READ SIDE TOO: a `DeployTargetPort` implementation `(environment) => DeployTarget | null` matching deploy-ports.ts:41, backed by this ledger. That is the edge that makes the module a real consumer rather than an exporter - the deploy engine already declares the port and waits for someone to write it.

`DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT_UNBOUND` (:46) is the answer when no target has been bound for an environment. Return it as a refusal with its layer, reusing an already-rostered layer literal - introduce no new `*_LAYER` constant, which would demand a security-roster backfill this row does not own.

No store construction, no clock, no spawn in this module beyond what the ledger seam already provides. `wc -l` and keep under 250.

REGISTER THE SYNCHRONOUS HANDLER (DoD 2). Add ONE entry to `GOAL_HANDLERS` in `apps/daemon/src/goals/goal-services.ts`.

APPEND IT - do not insert alphabetically. The table's own comment at :198 reads "Appended, never reordered: existing suites assert against this table's key order", and the current order is goal.create, goal.close, goal.create_with_source, repository.publish. Re-read HEAD first: this file is contended by task-537320ee.

The handler is SYNCHRONOUS, matching `CommandHandler = (context: HandlerContext) => ServiceOutcome` (bootstrap-ledger-vocabulary.ts:253). It: reads the payload, calls `admitDeployTargetPayload` (:99), refuses `DEPLOY_TARGET_INVALID` (:44) with its layer when admission returns null, and otherwise commits through the step-3 ledger.

DO NOT ADD IT TO THE ASYNC ENTRIES. `deployment.deploy` goes there because a deploy cannot be expressed synchronously; `deployment.set_target` is an ordinary durable write and bootstrap-contracts.ts:48 already records that distinction. Putting a sync write in the async seam would misrepresent it to every consumer that reasons about which kinds are long-running.

The registry composes GOAL_HANDLERS by spreading (daemon-command-registry.ts:194), so this needs NO registry edit - which matters, because that file is past its 400-line cap at the merge-base.

THE ADMISSION ARMS (DoD 3) - `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-target-contracts.test.ts`. This is the security half of the row and it is why the module was worth adopting rather than rewriting.

Every field is operator-typed text that reaches an argv (`--network <network>`, `ssh <sshTarget> docker ...`) or a rendered receipt. Assert each refusal with its CODE and its LAYER, never merely that it failed:
- A `url` carrying `user:password@` is REFUSED. A credential in a target lands on EVERY receipt that target produces, and receipts are durable and rendered - this is the arm that matters most.
- A `network` or `sshTarget` containing whitespace, a shell metacharacter, a newline or a NUL is REFUSED. The engine spawns with `shell: false` so a metacharacter cannot re-parse into a second command - say that in the note - but an unadmitted value still reaches a REMOTE HOST, which is the harm the regexes at :49/:51 guard.
- A `url` past MAX_URL (:52, 512) is refused; boundary-test at exactly 512 and 513.
- Assert the ACCEPTING cases too, or a regex that rejects everything passes every arm above.

THE PAYLOAD-KEY AGREEMENT ARM - the guard for the duplication this row cannot fix. `DEPLOYMENT_SET_TARGET_PAYLOAD_KEYS` (:30) and the hand-written literal in `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-payload-keys.ts:165` are two sources for one fact. Assert SET EQUALITY between them by IMPORTING both - reading that file is not editing it, so this stays inside rail 4. Do the same for the deploy keys (:37 vs :166). Without this, the two drift silently and the first symptom is a rejected payload nobody can explain.

Record in the step note that converging them (making daemon-command-payload-keys.ts import the constants) is a FOLLOW-UP, deferred because eight rows contend that file.

MUTATE AND CONFIRM RED: loosen `admitDeployUrl` to allow userinfo and confirm the credential arm reds; restore. The module is newly tracked, so prove the restore with `git diff -- <path>` once it is staged.

GATES AND SELF-REVIEW (DoD 5 and 6).

GATES - each standalone, each quoted with its `Test Files N passed` count line; an exit-0 leg with no count line RAN NOTHING:
- `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` (@moe/daemon is apps/daemon - resolve by PACKAGE NAME).
- `pnpm typecheck`.
State that root `pnpm test` covers NO apps/** file, so it is not evidence for anything this row owns. Respect the host's one-full-suite-at-a-time rule; prefer the filtered leg.

SCOPE EVIDENCE (DoD 5) - make it a command, not a sentence:
`git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-payload-keys.ts apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-contracts.ts` must be EMPTY. Those already carry both kinds and eight rows are contending them; an edit here is a collision, not thoroughness. `goal-services.ts` IS touched by this row - re-read HEAD before your final commit in case task-537320ee landed meanwhile.

SELF-REVIEW:
- Can a credential reach a receipt through any admitted field? Re-read `admitDeployUrl` and try `https://user:pass@host`, `https://user@host`, and a url with credentials in a query parameter - the last one the regex may not cover, and it is worth knowing which shapes are actually guarded.

- What happens if `projectId` is empty in `deployTargetAggregateId`? Two projects sharing an aggregate id would cross-bind targets.
- Did anything import the module ONLY from a test? That is not adoption (DoD 1).
